strengths: The paper addresses a relevant problem: improving robustness during parameter-efficient adaptation without increasing deployment-time model size.

The reported performance gains span mathematical reasoning, code generation, and GLUE. Relative to PiSSA, BA-LoRA improves GSM8K from 51.48 to 55.86, MBPP from 23.84 to 36.86, and average GLUE performance from 89.47 to 90.67.
The evaluation includes component ablations, extensions to LoRA and DoRA, rank and architecture comparisons, and explicit training-time and memory measurements.
weaknesses: The NLU spectral regularizer is incompatible with the stated experimental configuration. Equation (7) operates on an N-by-D class-logit matrix, but Section 3.1 sets k=5 while GLUE classification tasks have only two or three classes. The numerator is therefore undefined as indexed; if k is clipped to the available singular values, the ratio is identically one and provides no regularization gradient. This directly conflicts with Table 4's reported improvement from the SVD-only NLU configuration and requires reconciliation before the results can be trusted.

The NLG diversity objective has the opposite sign from its stated purpose. Equation (10) defines positive entropy, -sum(p log p), and Equation (12) minimizes it with a positive coefficient. This encourages concentrated predictions rather than diversity. Whether this is a manuscript error or an implementation error is unresolved, and the distinction materially affects the proposed mechanism and reproducibility.

The central claim of mitigating inherited pre-training noise is not established. Comparing RoBERTa with T5 is not a controlled noise experiment: architecture, pre-training objective, corpus composition, and fine-tuning configuration all differ. Appendix B additionally trains T5 for one epoch versus tens of epochs for RoBERTa. Greater improvement on T5 cannot isolate inherited noise. Likewise, imposing imbalance during downstream fine-tuning tests adaptation to downstream imbalance, not inheritance from pre-training.

The anti-collapse and bias-mitigation rationale lacks adequate support. Off-diagonal covariance minimization in Equation (5) also admits constant, collapsed representations as a minimum; unlike VICReg, it contains no variance-preservation constraint. Zero covariance does not establish statistical independence. The imbalance evidence consists of t-SNE visualizations and silhouette scores, without minority-class accuracy, balanced accuracy, or fairness measurements. These results do not substantiate the broader fairness and safety claims.

The NLU consistency objective is underspecified. Pre-trained DeBERTa and RoBERTa do not inherently provide meaningful downstream class distributions, yet Equation (4) assumes such a teacher. The construction and training status of its classification head are not explained. STS-B is a regression task, but the method specifies class-softmax KL and cross-entropy without a regression adaptation. Furthermore, distillation from the allegedly biased teacher needs evidence that it preserves useful knowledge without preserving the targeted biases.

The ablations do not validate the claimed decomposition or synergy. Table 4 reports downstream scores rather than direct measurements of knowledge retention, collapse, or noise sensitivity, and omits pairwise combinations. Appendix D.2's claim that the full model exceeds the sum of individual improvements is contradicted by Table 4: on GSM8K, the individual gains sum to 6.36 points, whereas the full improvement is 4.38 points.

The empirical breadth does not resolve the soundness concerns. Main baseline scores are imported from publications rather than established through a common evaluation pipeline, and the large-model comparisons lack detailed numerical results and uncertainty. Important implementation details remain unspecified, including the NLU teacher and the operational meaning of the two-phase regularization schedule; code is deferred until acceptance. The contribution largely combines existing regularization ideas with PiSSA, so reliable implementation and causal evidence are especially important.

strengths: The paper addresses an important problem: improving the robustness of parameter-efficient adaptation while retaining useful pre-trained capabilities.

Reported evaluations cover reasoning, code generation, instruction following, and GLUE, with additional architecture, rank, and quantization experiments. Reported gains include 55.86 versus 51.48 on GSM8K and 90.67 versus 89.47 average GLUE for BA-LoRA versus PiSSA.

The paper includes component ablations, experiments adding the regularizers to LoRA and DoRA, and explicit computational measurements. Table 5 usefully quantifies the additional memory and training time.
weaknesses: The NLU spectral regularizer is ineffective under the stated configuration. Equation (7) operates on an N-by-D class-logit matrix, but Section 3.1 sets k=5 while the GLUE classification tasks have only two or three classes. Summing the available top singular values therefore makes the ratio identically one, yielding zero regularization gradient; literal indexing beyond the available values is undefined. This directly undermines the claimed mechanism and makes the NLU improvement attributed to this term in Table 4 unexplained.

The NLG diversity objective has the opposite sign from its stated purpose. Equation (10) defines positive entropy, −sum p log p, and Equation (12) minimizes it with a positive coefficient. This encourages concentrated predictions rather than diversity. Whether this is an equation error or an implementation error must be resolved before the method and its ablations can be assessed reliably.

The NLU covariance penalty does not establish the claimed protection against representation collapse. Constant logits across all samples produce zero covariance and minimize Equation (5), including when every sample receives the same dominant-class prediction. Unlike a variance-preserving objective, off-diagonal decorrelation alone does not exclude collapse; nor does zero covariance imply statistical independence.

The central claim of mitigating inherited pre-training bias is not established. Comparing RoBERTa and T5 is not a controlled noise experiment: architecture, pre-training objective, corpus composition, and fine-tuning configurations all differ, and corpus noise is not measured. The MNLI imbalance experiment changes downstream training data rather than pre-training data. Its t-SNE plots and silhouette scores do not demonstrate improved minority-class accuracy or fairness. No direct demographic-bias evaluation supports the broader fairness and safety claims.

The proposed three-way decomposition remains a hypothesis rather than a validated framework. Generic downstream accuracy improvements do not isolate knowledge retention, collapse prevention, or noise suppression. Distilling from the allegedly biased pre-trained teacher could also preserve its biases. Moreover, Appendix D.2 claims that combined improvements exceed the sum of individual contributions, but Table 4 contradicts this: the individual GSM8K gains sum to 6.36 points, whereas the combined gain is 4.38 points.

Experimental provenance and reproducibility need clarification. Appendix B.3 states that main-table baselines are copied from prior publications, while Section 3.1 broadly describes all experiments as averaged over three specified seeds. The manuscript does not establish a uniformly rerun comparison. It also leaves important implementation details unresolved, including how pre-trained encoders supply task-class teacher logits, how the objectives handle STS-B regression, and the precise additional regularization schedules. Code is promised only upon acceptance, preventing inspection of the discrepancies between formulas and reported results.

The methodological novelty is primarily a combination of PiSSA initialization, distillation, decorrelation or entropy regularization, and spectral regularization. Stronger matched comparisons against simpler regularization alternatives and direct mechanism measurements are needed to establish a distinctive contribution. The reported performance gains are promising, but they do not compensate for the fundamental objective inconsistencies and unsupported central interpretation.

strengths: The paper addresses a relevant problem: improving the robustness of parameter-efficient adaptation while preserving pretrained capabilities.
Reported benchmark gains are substantial in several settings: BA-LoRA improves DeBERTa GLUE average from 89.47 to 90.67 over PiSSA and LLaMA-2-7B MBPP from 24.74 to 36.86 over CorDA++.

The evaluation covers NLU and NLG, multiple model families and adapter ranks, and quantized variants. Single-component ablations and extensions to LoRA and DoRA provide useful evidence of potential generality.
The computational analysis explicitly reports the additional cost: approximately 16% more memory and 12% more training time than PiSSA in the measured setting.
weaknesses: The NLU SVD regularizer is incompatible with the stated configuration. Equation 7 operates on N-by-D class logits, but Section 3.1 specifies k=5 while GLUE classification tasks have only two or three classes. The numerator is therefore either undefined or, with standard truncation, equals the denominator, yielding a constant loss of -1 with no useful gradient. This contradicts the improvement attributed to SVD-only regularization in Table 4 and requires an implementation-level explanation.

The NLG diversity objective has the wrong sign for its stated purpose. Equation 10 defines positive entropy, -sum(p log p), and Equation 12 minimizes it with a positive coefficient. This encourages concentrated predictions rather than increased diversity. Whether this is a typographical or implementation error is unresolved.

The central catastrophic-inheritance claim is not established. Comparing RoBERTa with T5 does not control pretraining noise: architecture, objectives, corpora, and fine-tuning schedules also differ substantially. The imbalance experiment changes downstream training data rather than pretraining data. Neither experiment isolates mitigation of inherited bias or demonstrates that LoRA exacerbates it relative to full fine-tuning.

The claimed fairness and robustness benefits lack direct behavioral evaluation. The imbalance study provides t-SNE plots and silhouette scores, but no minority-class accuracy, macro-F1, or worst-group performance. There are no direct demographic fairness measurements or controlled corruption tests supporting the broader bias-mitigation claims.

Other methodological details weaken the proposed mechanism. Covariance decorrelation alone does not prevent collapse, since constant logits also minimize Equation 5. The pretrained NLU teacher's task-specific classification head is unspecified, and the softmax/cross-entropy formulation does not explain handling STS-B regression. Distillation from a potentially biased teacher also needs justification as a bias-removal mechanism.

Comparison and reproducibility remain insufficiently controlled. Main-table baselines are imported from publications rather than rerun together, leaving uncertainty about preprocessing, evaluation, tuning budgets, and the provenance of reported seed variability. Code is deferred until acceptance, which is particularly consequential given the objective inconsistencies.

The contribution combines PiSSA with established regularization ideas, while the claimed principled decomposition and synergy are stronger than the evidence. Single-component ablations do not establish that all three components are necessary; pairwise or leave-one-out ablations and direct measurements of forgetting, collapse, and noise sensitivity are missing. Appendix D.2's claim of gains exceeding the sum of individual contributions is also contradicted by Table 4.

strengths: The paper addresses a relevant problem: improving robustness and knowledge retention during parameter-efficient adaptation. Output-space regularization is compatible with multiple adapter methods and preserves their deployment advantages.

The reported empirical gains are substantial across several tasks. BA-LoRA improves the average GLUE score from 89.47 to 90.67 over PiSSA and MBPP from 24.74 to 36.86 over CorDA++. Appendix experiments extend evaluation across model families, adapter ranks, and quantized settings.

The appendix provides useful evidence beyond standard task accuracy: minority-class recall improves from 26.4% with PiSSA to 61.7%, and Wikitext-2 perplexity after adaptation is closer to the pretrained model. Measured training time and memory also make the performance–cost tradeoff assessable.
weaknesses: A major mathematical inconsistency undermines the NLU method and ablation results. Equation 7 operates on N × D class logits, while Section 3.1 specifies k = 5. GLUE classification tasks have only two or three classes, so summing the available top-k singular values gives the entire spectrum: the ratio is identically one for nonzero logits and supplies no optimization signal. Nevertheless, Table 4 attributes a GLUE improvement to this regularizer alone. The actual implementation or stated formulation must be corrected and reconciled with these results.

The anti-collapse justification is incomplete. Equation 5 penalizes only off-diagonal covariance; constant predictions have zero covariance and therefore minimize this term. Unlike VICReg, there is no variance-preserving constraint. Meanwhile, Equation 12 is not equivalent to the NLU spectral ratio: its maximum is attained by k equal nonzero singular values with zero tail, rather than arbitrary concentration into fewer dominant components. Both spectral objectives operate on uncentered logits and can respond to prediction-invariant common logit shifts. These properties require analysis and targeted diagnostics before the proposed mechanisms are convincing.

The central claim of mitigating inherited pretraining bias is not established. RoBERTa versus T5 confounds corpus quality with architecture, objective, model size, and fine-tuning configuration, and corpus noise is not directly measured. The authors acknowledge this limitation, but continue making stronger claims elsewhere. The controlled imbalance experiment introduces imbalance during fine-tuning, so it demonstrates downstream imbalance robustness rather than inheritance from pretraining. No direct societal-bias or fairness evaluation supports the broader fairness claims.

The consistency objective preserves predictions from the same pretrained model whose biases the method intends to alleviate. The paper does not explain how useful knowledge is distinguished from inherited errors; references to reliable teacher signals are not implemented through a selection or weighting mechanism. For NLU, the teacher uses a shared downstream classification head, making it especially important to specify head training and gradient detachment and justify why its outputs constitute reliable pretrained knowledge.

Novelty is limited relative to the positioning. The paper explicitly acknowledges prior work combining consistency, covariance, and dominant-singular-value regularization in feature space. BA-LoRA primarily transfers these ideas to output logits, adds a focused entropy variant for generation, and combines them with PiSSA. A direct comparison with that prior regularization framework and simple alternatives such as label smoothing or conventional distillation would better establish the contribution.

The evaluation does not adequately establish the claimed three-way mechanism or synergy. Table 4 includes individual regularizers but no leave-one-out combinations or mechanism-specific measurements. Appendix D.4 claims the combined gain exceeds the sum of individual gains, which Table 4 contradicts: on GSM8K the combined improvement is 4.38 points, versus 6.84 points summed across individual improvements. Main baseline scores are imported from publications, limiting confidence in exact comparability despite the stated recipe matching.

Important reproducibility details remain unresolved. STS-B is regression, but the NLU formulation assumes class softmax distributions and cross-entropy, without explaining its regression adaptation. The additional two-phase regularization schedule lacks a precise definition, and evaluation prompts, decoding settings, and randomized-SVD settings are insufficiently specified. The promised code link is missing from the supplied manuscript. These gaps are particularly consequential given the discrepancy between the NLU spectral objective and its reported results.

strengths: The paper addresses a relevant problem: improving robustness and preserving pretrained capabilities during parameter-efficient adaptation. Output-space regularization can be applied across multiple adapter parameterizations.

The reported empirical coverage is broad, including reasoning, code generation, GLUE, multiple model families, quantization, and adapter ranks. Tables 1–3 report substantial improvements, particularly on MBPP and CoLA.

The appendix provides useful evidence beyond standard task accuracy: minority-class recall improves from 26.4% with PiSSA to 61.7% with BA-LoRA under MNLI imbalance, and Wikitext-2 perplexity remains closer to the pretrained model. Component ablations and measured computational overhead are also valuable.
weaknesses: The stated NLU spectral regularizer has a serious mathematical inconsistency. Equation (7) operates on N-by-D class logits, but Section 3.1 sets k=5, whereas GLUE classification tasks have only two or three classes. Summing the available top-k singular values therefore includes the entire spectrum, making the ratio identically one and its gradient zero for nonzero matrices; without clipping, k exceeds the available spectrum. This cannot explain the reported GLUE improvement from adding only this regularizer in Table 4. The implementation and results require reconciliation.

The proposed failure-mode interpretation is insufficiently justified. Equation (5) penalizes off-diagonal covariance, but constant predictions already achieve zero covariance; without a variance constraint, this term does not itself prevent collapse. Moreover, covariance and spectral penalties on raw logits depend on class-independent logit shifts that leave predictions unchanged. The paper needs evidence that these objectives improve meaningful predictive structure rather than merely changing logit parameterization.

The central claim of mitigating inherited pretraining noise is not established. RoBERTa and T5 differ in architecture, pretraining objective, corpus size, and fine-tuning configurations, and their noise levels are not measured. The authors acknowledge this confounding, but still draw strong conclusions elsewhere. Artificially imbalancing downstream MNLI tests adaptation to downstream skew, while Wikitext-2 tests retention; neither isolates inherited bias. No direct societal-bias or fairness benchmark supports the broader fairness claims.

Novelty relative to the closest prior work is limited and insufficiently tested. Section 4 acknowledges that Chen et al. already combine consistency, covariance, and dominant-singular-value regularization for noisy pretraining. Moving analogous objectives to logits and combining them with PiSSA is a plausible extension, but the paper lacks a direct comparison against that feature-space approach and strong conventional regularization alternatives.

The consistency mechanism does not distinguish reliable pretrained knowledge from inherited bias. Despite language about reliable teacher signals, Equations (4) and (9) contain no reliability filtering. For NLU, the teacher uses a shared task-specific classification head rather than an established pretrained classifier, weakening the interpretation as preservation of pretrained task decisions. STS-B's regression setting is also not reconciled with the stated softmax/KL and cross-entropy formulation.

Experimental attribution remains incomplete. Main baseline results are imported from prior publications rather than rerun under one verified pipeline. Single-component ablations show potential utility but do not establish the claimed three-way synergy or each component's specific mechanism; pairwise combinations and targeted noise experiments are missing. Appendix D.4's claim that the combined improvement exceeds the sum of individual improvements is contradicted by Table 4.

Reproducibility is insufficient to resolve these concerns: the promised code link is absent, the two-phase regularization schedule is not precisely defined, and details of randomized-SVD differentiation and benchmark decoding are incomplete. Given the objective/result inconsistency and unsupported central attribution, the reported gains are not sufficient for acceptance.

strengths: The paper addresses an important practical problem: improving robustness and knowledge retention during parameter-efficient adaptation. Output-space regularization is compatible with several LoRA variants.

The reported evaluation is broad, covering NLU, mathematical reasoning, coding, multiple model families, adapter ranks, and quantization. Reported improvements include a 1.20-point GLUE gain over PiSSA and substantial gains on code generation.

The minority-class recall results and Wikitext-2 perplexity evaluation provide useful evidence beyond aggregate task accuracy. Computational measurements also quantify the additional training and memory costs.
weaknesses: A major inconsistency undermines the NLU spectral regularizer. Equation 7 operates on an N×D class-logit matrix, while Section 3.1 specifies k=5. The GLUE classification tasks have only two or three classes, so there are fewer than five singular values. Clipping k to the available spectrum makes the ratio identically one and its gradient zero; otherwise, the formula is undefined. This cannot explain the reported improvement from the SVD-only NLU ablation in Table 4. The implemented objective and results need reconciliation.

The anti-collapse justification is incomplete. Equation 5 penalizes only off-diagonal covariance; constant predictions also achieve zero loss. Unlike VICReg, this objective lacks a variance-preserving term, so it does not itself prevent collapse. Additionally, Appendix C.5 describes its entropy comparator as entropy minimization, whereas the NLG objective maximizes entropy, weakening the claimed comparison between diversity objectives.

The central claim about mitigating inherited pre-training bias is not established. RoBERTa versus T5 confounds corpus quality with architecture, pre-training objective, and adaptation configuration, as the appendix acknowledges. Artificially imbalancing downstream MNLI demonstrates resilience to fine-tuning imbalance, but does not isolate inherited bias or show that low-rank adaptation amplifies it. No direct societal-fairness evaluation supports the broader fairness claims.

The consistency mechanism needs stronger justification and implementation detail. For NLU, the teacher uses a newly attached, shared task-specific classification head, rather than an established pre-trained classifier. Its initialization, updates, and gradient handling are insufficiently specified. No reliability filtering implements the text's qualification about trustworthy teacher signals. STS-B is also not addressed: with a conventional scalar regression output, the softmax KL and off-diagonal covariance terms are vacuous.

Novelty and component necessity are insufficiently demonstrated. The related-work section acknowledges prior work combining consistency, covariance, and dominant-singular-value regularization; the principal changes are their application to output logits and PEFT, with task-specific variants. Comparisons against that framework and simpler regularization alternatives are missing. Single-component ablations do not establish that all three terms are necessary without leave-one-out combinations. The claim that the full method exceeds the sum of individual gains is contradicted by Table 4.

Experimental comparability and reproducibility remain uncertain. Main baselines are imported from other publications rather than rerun, and the manuscript does not fully establish matched decoding, checkpoint selection, and tuning budgets. This particularly matters for the unusually large MBPP gain. The arithmetic NLG average mixes percentage metrics with a differently scaled MT-Bench score. Several schedule details remain underspecified, and the code-availability statements contain no usable repository link.
